messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Automatic chunk label generation
parts:
Hi,

Is there any option to force the automatic chunk label generation?
Now empty label ("") are generated for the chunk without label,
but perhaps each chunk should have an unique label.

kohske

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Automatic chunk label generation
parts:
Chunks without labels are assigned labels of the form unnamed-chunk-i
(http://yihui.name/knitr/options), e.g.

library(knitr)
knit(text = '<<>>=
1+1
@
')

|>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> | 50%
label: unnamed-chunk-1
|>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>| 100%
ordinary text without R code


Regards,
Yihui
--

Thanks,
I found that this happens in markdown and for chunk with options.

> knit(text = '```{r, prompt = TRUE}
+ 1+1
+ ```
+ ')
|>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> | 50%
label: (with options)
List of 1
$ prompt: logi TRUE

chunk "" is empty or set not to be evaluated

|>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>| 100%
ordinary text without R code

|>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> | 50%
label: unnamed-chunk-1
|>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>| 100%
ordinary text without R code

```r
1 + 1
```



```

```

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Automatic chunk label generation
parts:
Oh, that is because the syntax is not quite right; you should put a
space instead of a comma afer ```{r before you write chunk options.

knit(text = '```{r prompt = TRUE}
1+1
```
')

This is subtle. I may change the rule so that ```{r,} is also allowed
if other people also run into this problem. Thanks for the feedback!

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Automatic chunk label generation

Oh, thanks. It works.
In my view, maybe it is natural to use {r, options} rather than {r options}.

Now I understand the design.

```{r x=1, hoge, y = 2}
1+1
```
hoge is label, and other two args are options.
So args are params if it is the form of x=y, and label otherwise, right?

> This is subtle. I may change the rule so that ```{r,} is also allowed
> if other people also run into this problem. Thanks for the feedback!

good.

thanks,

kohske

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Automatic chunk label generation
parts:
Labels are treated differently only due to laziness. Strictly
speaking, you should write ```{r label='foo', x=1}, but ```{r foo,
x=1} also works so we can save some typing efforts.

The space syntax ```{r options} actually came from Github and Pandoc's
markdown; the space is used to separate the language name with other
options.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>

Ok,

first I misunderstood that the syntax is

```{r [label] [[,] options]}

but now I understand that label is also an option. So syntax is

```{r [options]}

and

options := option, option, ...

it does make sense.

thanks.
